sections.title: Commercial roofing for a growing Mission
paras: Mission's commercial side is growing on both ends. Along Expressway 83 at Bryan Rd, the Mission Gateway development is part of what the Mission EDC calls the Bryan corridor. To the south, Sharyland Business Park has room for about 2.5 million square feet of industrial space near the Anzalduas International Bridge, and the bridge's $88 million expansion adds six commercial lanes. Older buildings along Business 83 and the expressway fill in the rest.

That mix means two kinds of commercial roof jobs. New warehouses and stores need a membrane system installed right the first time. Older buildings from earlier decades need repairs, coatings, or full replacement as their roofs age out.
We drive to Mission from our office at 1815 N Jackson Rd in Edinburg, about 26 minutes. We have worked on commercial roofs across Hidalgo County since 2003.

sections.title: Wind and rain on Mission's flat roofs
paras: Mission has had dangerous wind more than once. On May 31, 2016, a downburst near Palmview and Mission brought winds the NWS estimated at 85 to 95 mph and damaged more than 150 homes and businesses. On April 29, 2023, wind flipped food trucks near Bryan Rd and Business 83, close to City Hall, while the McAllen airport recorded a 74 mph gust.
Wind like that pulls at the edges of a flat roof. If the perimeter metal or the membrane seams are loose, the roof can peel back from the edge. Rooftop units and their curbs are another weak point.

Rain is the other test. Hurricane Hanna dropped 14.40 inches on Mission in July 2020. A flat roof only handles that much water if the drains, scuppers, and gutters are open and the roof slopes to them. Ponding water left on a roof for days works into seams and ages the membrane early.

cards.title: New flat roof systems
cards.body: TPO, EPDM, and modified bitumen installed on new buildings and additions, coordinated with your builder or general contractor.

cards.title: Roof replacement
cards.body: Old system torn off, decking checked and repaired, new membrane installed on a written timeline.

cards.title: Leak repair
cards.body: We trace leaks to the seam, flashing, or drain where water actually gets in and repair it there.

cards.title: Edge and flashing repair
cards.body: Loose perimeter metal and flashing secured after wind, before the next storm can lift the membrane.

cards.title: Roof coatings
cards.body: A reflective coating can add years to a sound, aging roof. See roof coatings in Mission.

cards.title: Inspections
cards.body: Routine and after storm inspections with a written report and photos for owners and managers.

sections.title: Code and planning for commercial work in Mission
paras: The City of Mission's permit paperwork lists the 2024 International Building Code and the matching 2024 codes for fire, plumbing, mechanical, and energy. For questions about a permit on your building, call the Inspections Division at (956) 580-8691.

Commercial work needs more planning than a house. Tenants are affected, deliveries still have to come in, and some jobs need to happen in stages. We inspect before we estimate, put everything in writing, and schedule around your building. If you manage several Mission properties, we can set up recurring inspections so small problems get fixed before they turn into a replacement.

faqs.q: We are building a new warehouse near the bridge. Can you roof it?
faqs.a: Yes. We install TPO, EPDM, and modified bitumen systems on new commercial buildings and work with your builder or general contractor on the schedule.

faqs.q: The 2016 or 2023 wind loosened our roof edge. Is that a repair or a new roof?
faqs.a: Often a repair, if the membrane and insulation underneath are still dry and sound. We check the edge, the seams, and the insulation, and the written scope tells you which one it is.

faqs.q: Water sits on our flat roof after it rains. Is that a problem?
faqs.a: Water that is gone within a day or two is normal on many flat roofs. Water that stays longer points to a low spot or a blocked drain, and over time it ages the membrane and finds seams. We can find the cause and fix the drainage.

faqs.q: How long does a commercial roof last in Mission?
faqs.a: A well installed membrane in the RGV typically lasts 15 to 25 years, depending on the material and the upkeep. Heat and UV shorten it; regular inspections help it go longer.

faqs.q: Do you inspect commercial roofs after a storm?
faqs.a: Yes. After high wind or hail we walk the roof, check the edges, seams, flashing, and rooftop units, and give you a written report with photos for your insurer. We are not a public adjuster, so the claim is between you and your insurance company.

faqs.q: Can you work around our tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. We schedule around tenant hours and give you documentation for insurance and maintenance records when the job is done.

faqs.q: How do I get a commercial estimate in Mission?
faqs.a: Call (956) 422-3335 or book an inspection online. We walk the roof, take measurements, and give you a free written estimate.
